panels.title: Public API
panels.description: Blackbox probe of /healthz every 2m -- the liveness signal.

panels.title: Data volume
panels.description: From helpers/volume_guard.sh via the node-exporter textfile collector. 0 means Postgres may be on an empty root-disk cluster while /healthz still returns ok.

panels.title: Scrape targets up
panels.description: blackbox-stats is EXCLUDED: it scrapes every 20m, so its series is stale for most of that window and would make this flap between 5 and 6. Its health is covered by its own alert.

panels.title: Cert expires in
panels.description: tls internal issues 12-HOUR certs, so ~9-12h here is NORMAL. Alert threshold is deliberately 1h.

panels.title: OOM kills (1h)
panels.description: Host has ZERO swap - OOM kills are abrupt.

panels.title: Cache entries
panels.description: Baseline 2026-08-22: 465,433. A collapse here is the data-side signature of the volume boot race.

panels.title: A3M total
panels.description: Sum of a3m_size_bytes over status IN ('active','held') entries -- both keep their OSDF object; only 'stale' rows have been reclaimed.

panels.title: Capacity used
panels.description: Against 50 TB (decimal). If the quota is actually TiB, this reads ~10% high.

panels.title: Projected time to full
panels.description: Linear extrapolation of the last 7 days of growth. Needs about a week of history to mean anything; negative or absent means storage is flat or shrinking.

panels.title: Growth / day
panels.description: Bytes added per day, from the same 7d linear fit.

panels.title: A3M bytes by source
panels.description: Stacked, so the top of the stack is total consumption.

panels.title: Capacity used (%)
panels.description: Watch the slope, not the value -- at 5.9% the slope is what tells you when to ask for more quota.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio (all time)
panels.description: The headline number. hits/sequences, both counted per SEQUENCE. Note the query_metrics table cannot produce this: its `count` is per-REQUEST while `hit_count` is per-sequence, so the two columns are different units.

panels.title: 5xx rate (24h)
panels.description: `or vector(0)` matters: with no 5xx at all the numerator has no series and the panel would read 'No data', which is ambiguous on an error-rate tile -- you cannot tell 0% from broken. clamp_min avoids divide-by-zero on a quiet day.

panels.title: OSDF verify in-flight
panels.description: Compare with verify_concurrency (4). Pinned at 4 with a flat fetch rate is the signature of a hung `pelican object get` -- the timeout covers only the queue wait, not the fetch.

panels.title: DB pool checked out
panels.description: Saturation is 60 (pool_size 20 + max_overflow 40).

panels.title: Token issue failures
panels.description: `pelican token create` has no timeout and no retry. If this climbs, no OSPool job can upload -- while /healthz stays green.

panels.title: Application errors by code
panels.description: AppError.code. 4xx codes (already_cached, upload_too_large) are client behaviour, not incidents; osdf_unavailable and token_issuance_failed are.

panels.title: Classifier outcomes
panels.description: 'unclassified' is a real no-hit. binary_missing / timeout / nonzero_exit mean diamond is broken -- previously invisible, since every failure path silently returns UNCLASSIFIED.

panels.title: Probe latency (/healthz 2m, /v1/stats 20m)
panels.description: /v1/stats is ~50x more expensive than /healthz (8 scalar subqueries over a 465k-row table), which is why it is probed at 20m. Its line is sparse by design.

panels.title: Reaper exposure - INFORMATIONAL ONLY (job is NOT scheduled)
panels.description: Entries past their source's idle_ttl_days that the reaper WOULD delete if enabled. It is deliberately NOT scheduled: on this instance reap() issues real `pelican object rm`. Read-only count.

panels.title: Classified (active entries)
panels.description: Share of ACTIVE cache entries with a real species + protein name. The rest are 'Pending Classification' (waiting on the NR-BLAST box) or 'Unclassified'.

panels.title: Pending classification (%)
panels.description: ACTIVE entries still carrying the 'Pending Classification' sentinel in both fields -- exactly the set helpers/reclassify_export.sh ships nightly (minus those under RECLASS_EXPORT_MIN_LENGTH aa). Should trend down while jobs post results.

panels.title: Pending entries
panels.description: Count behind the percentage. Re-ingesting a sequence re-arms the sentinel, so this never reaches zero while uploads keep arriving.

panels.title: Unclassified (active)
panels.description: Either field literally 'Unclassified'. NOT part of the NR-BLAST pipeline (its callback only updates both-pending rows); mostly rows with a known species but no protein name.

panels.title: Reclass jobs active
panels.description: reclass_jobs rows QUEUED or RUNNING on the BLAST box. >0 means reclassify_poll.sh is polling every 10 min; 0 means it exits without opening ssh.

panels.title: Reclass jobs failed
panels.description: FAILED + KILLED + UNKNOWN jobs, all time. The reason is in reclass_jobs.last_status.log_tail (GET /v1/admin/classification/jobs).

panels.title: Classification state (% of active entries)
panels.description: Stacked to 100%: classified vs pending vs unclassified. Watch pending fall after each nightly job; a step up is a bulk ingest arriving.

panels.title: Pending / unclassified entries (count)
panels.description: The absolute backlog the NR-BLAST pipeline works through. Each DONE job should show as a drop in `pending`; the slope between jobs is the upload rate.

panels.title: Host memory available
panels.description: Zero swap on this host, so this is the OOM precursor.

panels.title: Ingestions logged in the last 5s
panels.description: New POST /v1/uploads/request calls in a trailing 5s window (increase() over af3cache_http_requests_total, at the 1s af3cache-api scrape interval). Same pattern as "Queries in the last 5s". Replaces a prior version that read the current pending/uploaded row-count backlog from postgres-exporter (af3cache_ingestions_count) -- that snapshot is still available (only scraped every 30s) if backlog size, not request-logging rate, is what's needed.

panels.title: Ingestion requests/s
panels.description: Throughput of the upload endpoints (POST /v1/uploads/request and POST /v1/uploads/{ingestion_id}/complete), averaged over a trailing 5s window at the 1s af3cache-api scrape interval. Previously averaged over the dashboard's selected time range ($__range), which smoothed out short bursts over a multi-hour view.

panels.title: Query requests/s
panels.description: Throughput of POST /v1/query, averaged over a trailing 5s window at the 1s af3cache-api scrape interval. Previously averaged over the dashboard's selected time range ($__range), which smoothed out short bursts over a multi-hour view.

panels.title: Queries in the last 5s
panels.description: Completed /v1/query requests in a trailing 5s window (increase() over af3cache_http_requests_total, at the 1s af3cache-api scrape interval). Switched from a raw af3cache_query_inflight gauge reading: /v1/query resolves in low milliseconds (see the duration histogram), so true concurrency almost never holds above 0/1 between scrapes even under heavy load -- this counts completed requests instead of sampling instantaneous concurrency, which is what actually shows burst volume. af3cache_query_inflight is still exposed (unpanelled) for spotting a genuinely hung request, the way af3cache_osdf_verify_inflight does for OSDF fetches.

panels.title: In-flight ingestions by age
panels.description: pending + uploaded rows by age. The sweeper (helpers/sweep_ingestions.sh, every 15 min) re-attempts everything over 30 min and expires what is still unverifiable past 24 h, so over_24h should stay at 0.

panels.title: Sweeper outcomes (per hour)
panels.description: af3cache_ingestion_sweep_total by outcome. published = abandoned upload rescued; expired = rejected as 'Expired - Upload unverifiable' past 24 h; unverified = retried next run; expiries_held = OSDF-outage breaker engaged; error = see api log.
